title: Topology
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn point-set topology and a first look at algebraic topology: topological spaces and bases, closure and interior, continuous maps and homeomorphisms, subspace, product and quotient topologies, connectedness and path connectedness, compactness, countability and separation axioms, Urysohn's lemma and metrization in outline, and homotopy and the fundamental group of the circle.
primary_reading: Topology Without Tears by Sidney A. Morris (free PDF)

weeks.1: Topological spaces, open sets and bases
weeks.2: Closed sets, closure, interior and limit points
weeks.7: Compactness of finite products and compactness in metric spaces
weeks.10: Metrization in outline and the Cantor set
weeks.12: The fundamental group of the circle and its applications

blocks.deliverable: Decide which supplied collections are topologies and find closures and interiors.
Show that a supplied quotient space is homeomorphic to a familiar space.
Prove that supplied spaces are or are not connected or compact.
Week 7 midterm; prove a separation property of a supplied space.
Use Urysohn's lemma to separate disjoint closed sets by a continuous function.
Prove the two-dimensional Brouwer fixed point theorem from the fundamental group of the circle.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Counterexample atlas: build a written atlas of twelve spaces (including the Sorgenfrey line, the topologist's sine curve, the Cantor set and the line with two origins) that shows exactly which properties each has and lacks, with proofs, and write a full proof that the fundamental group of the circle is the integers, with two applications.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
